policy_selection: Maximize the smaller mean food score of NanoJev and Jev; break ties by their mean food score, then survival rate, then greedy. Apply one selected policy to all compared systems.
case_selection: Outcome-selected highlight: require NanoJev and Jev to survive the complete 256-step horizon while the original Qwen run becomes trapped; among eligible cases prefer the largest minimum NanoJev/Jev food score, then their mean food score.
maze_selection: Fixed existing 50x50 OOD case; deterministic model-guided local-edge exploration, not stochastic action sampling.
common_snake_code: Filter immediate collisions; retain actions on shortest static safe food paths when available; model ranks remaining ties; forced moves use code.
original_case_selection: Among shared cases in the selected policy, maximize minimum NanoJev/Jev food score, then their mean food score, then the food-score gap above the native baseline. Preserve complete recorded episodes and label the result as a selected showcase, not a cohort average.

selection_revision.timing: After examining greedy outcomes; this is an editorial showcase selection, not a preregistered model-quality estimate.
selection_revision.reason: The user requested the most interesting complete game example and previously specified successful NanoJev/Jev runs with a failing untuned baseline. All eight-case controller results remain in the comparison summary.
